exposure: premature rupture of membranes (PROM) >= 18 hours or concurrent maternal fever
maternal-infant blood type incompatibility with positive direct Coombs test
cohort: 646 neonates born at the Second Hospital of Dalian Medical University between January 2021 and January 2024 were included in the study.
finding: A nomogram constructed from six independent factors (GA, BW, PROM, maternal-infant blood type incompatibility, probiotic supplementation, and weight loss) demonstrated good differentiation, calibration, and clinical applicability for predicting neonatal hyperbilirubinemia.
